headline: Saclag Reaches Asian Games MMA Final; Alvarez Finishes With Bronze
seoTitle: Saclag Reaches Asian Games MMA Final, Alvarez Takes Bronze | FMB News
seoDescription: Jean Claude Saclag advanced to the Asian Games men's traditional -65kg MMA gold-medal match while Carlos Alvarez completed his -77kg campaign with bronze.
deck: Saclag beat Japan's Daisuke Murayama 3-0 in the -65kg semifinal to guarantee at least silver, while Alvarez's -77kg run ended with bronze after a 0-3 semifinal loss to Kazakhstan's Yerkingali Burkutalin.
author: FMB News Sports Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Jean Claude Saclag advanced to the men's traditional -65kg mixed martial arts final at the 2026 Asian Games after defeating Japan's Daisuke Murayama, 3-0, in Monday's semifinal at Nagoya City Inae Sports Center.
The victory upgrades Saclag's guaranteed medal from at least bronze to at least silver. He is scheduled to face Tajikistan's Otabek Rajabov in Tuesday's gold-medal match.
Carlos Alvarez, meanwhile, completed his men's traditional -77kg campaign with bronze after losing 0-3 to Kazakhstan's Yerkingali Burkutalin in the semifinal.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: GMA News, the Philippine Daily Inquirer and The Philippine Star independently reported Saclag's semifinal victory and Alvarez's bronze-medal finish. The official Aichi-Nagoya competition schedule confirms September 21 as the MMA semifinal session and September 22 as the final and medal-ceremony session.
Saclag has not yet won gold. His confirmed result at this stage is a place in the final and a guaranteed minimum silver medal.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: This is an independently newsworthy continuation of FMB News' September 21 report, 'Saclag, Alvarez Assure Philippines of Two Asian Games MMA Medals,' which covered their quarterfinal victories and guaranteed minimum bronzes before the semifinals. Earliest FMB News report: /news/saclag-alvarez-assured-asian-games-mma-medals-september-21-2026.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Saclag is one victory away from the Philippines' first gold medal of these Asian Games and from a gold in mixed martial arts in the sport's Asian Games debut. Alvarez has now converted his guaranteed quarterfinal medal into a confirmed bronze finish.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Saclag faces Otabek Rajabov of Tajikistan in the -65kg final on September 22. The result will determine whether his medal is gold or silver.

verificationNotes: The Aichi-Nagoya organising committee's official venue schedule confirms MMA semifinals on September 21 and finals on September 22 at Nagoya City Inae Sports Center.
GMA News reports Alvarez's 0-3 semifinal loss and bronze medal and states that Saclag advanced to the final after a 3-0 semifinal win over Daisuke Murayama.
INQUIRER.net and The Philippine Star independently corroborate Saclag's final qualification; The Philippine Star also corroborates Alvarez's bronze finish.
The article does not describe Saclag as a gold medalist; gold remains contingent on the September 22 final.
This article links explicitly to the earliest relevant FMB News report from September 21.
The contextual venue photograph is KKPCW's own work on Wikimedia Commons under CC BY-SA 4.0 and is clearly labeled as a 2020 file photograph.
